documents.title: H&P - Admission, COPD Exacerbation
lines: ADMISSION H&P
Time of eval: 03:45, HD1
CHIEF COMPLAINT: shortness of breath x 3 days, worse overnight
HPI:
82 yo female with severe COPD on home 2L NC, HFrEF, HTN, T2DM presents with progressive dyspnea, cough with thick yellow sputum.
Symptoms began 3 days ago after URI in household. Increased home albuterol MDI q2h without relief. No fever reported at home.
EMS called at 01:05 for work of breathing.
SpO2 84% at triage; required 4L NC to reach SpO2 89%.
Three albuterol-ipratropium nebulizers given in the ED between 01:40 and 03:00 plus methylprednisolone 125 mg IV; persistent diffuse wheeze and dyspnea at rest afterward.
Somnolent on arrival, arousable to voice but falls asleep mid-sentence; wife reports this is new today.
Also reports 3 kg weight increase this week and worsening leg swelling; has been missing evening diuretic doses.
Denies chest pain, hemoptysis, orthopnea beyond baseline 2 pillows, calf pain.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
COPD GOLD stage 3, 2 exacerbations in past 12 months, 1 prior hospitalization
History of heart failure with ejection fraction 30%; bilateral leg edema and 3 kg weight increase this week.
Type 2 diabetes, last A1c 7.4
Hypertension
Former smoker, 50 pack-years, quit 9 years ago
Osteoporosis
HOME MEDICATIONS:
Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily
Budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 two puffs BID
Albuterol MDI 2 puffs q4h PRN
Furosemide 40 mg PO daily
Carvedilol 6.25 mg PO BID
Lisinopril 10 mg PO daily
Metformin 500 mg PO BID
Home O2 2L NC at night
ALLERGIES: sulfa - rash
SOCIAL: lives with wife in single-story home, uses rollator, daughter nearby, no recent travel.
EXAM:
Vitals 03:50: T 37.4, HR 112 irregular-regular, BP 148/82, RR 32, SpO2 90% on 4L NC
General: ill-appearing, sitting upright at edge of bed
Visible accessory muscle use with tripod positioning; respiratory rate 32; speaking 2 to 3 words at a time.
Neuro: arousable to voice, oriented to self and place, closes eyes when not stimulated, no focal deficit, no asterixis noted at this time
HEENT: dry mucous membranes, no JVD appreciated at 30 degrees due to body habitus
Lungs: diffuse expiratory wheeze bilaterally, prolonged expiratory phase, decreased air movement at bases
CV: tachycardic, regular, soft systolic murmur at apex, no rub
Abd: soft, nontender, no hepatomegaly
Ext: 2+ pitting edema to mid-shin bilaterally, warm, no cords
Skin: no rash
LABS/STUDIES:
WBC 13.2, Hgb 12.8, Plt 244
Na 137, K 4.1, Cr 1.1, BUN 24, glucose 188
BNP 640, troponin 0.03 flat on repeat
CXR: hyperinflation, flattened diaphragms, mild pulmonary vascular congestion, no focal consolidation, no pneumothorax
ECG: sinus tachycardia 110, no acute ST changes
ASSESSMENT:
82 yo F with acute COPD exacerbation, likely viral/bacterial trigger, with superimposed volume overload and hypoxemic respiratory distress.
PLAN:
1. COPD: scheduled albuterol-ipratropium nebs q4h and q2h PRN, continue inhaled maintenance once stable
2. IV steroid: methylprednisolone 40 mg IV every 8 hours; glucose rose to 342 requiring insulin sliding scale.
3. Azithromycin 500 mg IV x1 then 250 mg daily
4. O2 to keep SpO2 88-92%, wean as tolerated
5. HFrEF: hold home furosemide dose, give furosemide 40 mg IV BID, daily weights, strict I/O
6. Hold metformin, q4h fingersticks with sliding scale insulin
7. Continue carvedilol at reduced dose if BP allows, hold lisinopril pending renal function
8. Neuro checks q2h given somnolence, limit sedating meds
9. Telemetry, admit to stepdown, RT at bedside, code status full per pt and wife

documents.title: Progress Note HD2 - AM Rounds
lines: PROGRESS NOTE HD2, 07:20
SUBJECTIVE:
Pt more alert this morning, answering in short sentences, no longer falling asleep mid-sentence. Slept in recliner position. Cough looser, sputum now lighter.
Reports dyspnea improved from admission but still winded with transfer to commode.
Wife at bedside overnight, states pt looks closer to baseline mentally.
OBJECTIVE:
Weight 71.2 kg, down 0.8 kg from admission. Net -1.3 L over 24h. UOP 1850 mL.
Exam: sitting upright, no tripod posture this morning, mild intercostal retraction only
Lungs: expiratory wheeze still diffuse but improved air movement, no crackles at bases
CV: RRR, no new murmur
Ext: 2+ edema bilaterally, unchanged
Labs: WBC 11.4, Na 138, K 3.8, Cr 1.0, BNP not repeated
Fingersticks overnight: 244, 298, 342 at 04:00 - glucose rose to 342 requiring insulin sliding scale.
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
1. COPD exacerbation - improving. Continue albuterol-ipratropium nebs q4h, q2h PRN. Restart maintenance inhalers today.
2. Steroid: continue methylprednisolone 40 mg IV q8h today, plan transition to PO prednisone HD3 if trajectory holds.
3. Hyperglycemia steroid-induced - increase to moderate sliding scale, add glargine 8 units qHS, q4h FSBG. Metformin remains held.
4. HFrEF EF 30% - continue furosemide 40 mg IV BID, daily weights, K repletion 40 mEq PO today.
5. O2 wean by 1L as tolerated targeting SpO2 88-92%.
6. Continue azithromycin, day 2 of 5.
7. PT/OT consult for mobility and home safety eval.
8. Mentation improved, continue q4h neuro checks today.
Discussed plan with pt and wife at bedside 07:40.

documents.title: Progress Note HD5
lines: PROGRESS NOTE HD5, 08:05
SUBJECTIVE:
Pt reports she feels near her usual baseline. Walked hallway 45 feet with RN and rollator yesterday evening without stopping.
Speaking in full sentences. No orthopnea. Appetite improved, ate most of breakfast.
No nocturnal dyspnea overnight per RN.
OBJECTIVE:
T 36.9, HR 82, BP 128/70, RR 18, SpO2 93% on 2L NC, 90% on room air ambulating
Weight 68.9 kg, total 3.1 kg down from admission. Net -3.9 L LOS.
Exam: comfortable, no accessory muscle use, no tripod positioning
Lungs: scattered faint end-expiratory wheeze, good air movement throughout
CV: RRR, no gallop appreciated
Ext: trace edema at ankles bilaterally, much improved
Labs: WBC 8.1, Na 139, K 4.0, Cr 0.9, glucose 176 and 194 today
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
1. COPD exacerbation - near resolved. Nebs spaced to q6h, PRN q4h. Maintenance tiotropium and budesonide-formoterol continued, inhaler technique reviewed with RT.
2. Steroid taper: prednisone 40 mg PO daily, plan 5 more days total then stop.
3. Steroid hyperglycemia improving, glargine reduced to 5 units qHS, continue FSBG QID, plan to resume metformin at discharge.
4. HFrEF EF 30% - transition to furosemide 40 mg PO daily today, monitor weight and Cr. Restart lisinopril 10 mg daily.
5. Azithromycin course completed HD5.
6. O2: trial off during day, keep home 2L nocturnal.
7. PT cleared for home with rollator and daughter assistance.
8. Anticipate discharge HD6 if maintains SpO2 off O2 with ambulation.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - COPD Exacerbation
lines: DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit HD1, discharged HD6. LOS 6 days.
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSES:
1. Acute exacerbation of COPD with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure
2. Acute on chronic HFrEF exacerbation
3. Steroid-induced hyperglycemia
4. Type 2 diabetes, hypertension
HOSPITAL COURSE:
82 yo female with severe COPD and HFrEF presented overnight with 3 days of worsening dyspnea and productive cough.
SpO2 84% at triage; required 4L NC to reach SpO2 89%.
Three albuterol-ipratropium nebulizers given in the ED between 01:40 and 03:00 plus methylprednisolone 125 mg IV; persistent diffuse wheeze and dyspnea at rest afterward.
On admission exam: Visible accessory muscle use with tripod positioning; respiratory rate 32; speaking 2 to 3 words at a time.
Somnolent on arrival, arousable to voice but falls asleep mid-sentence; wife reports this is new today. Mentation returned to baseline by HD2 with treatment.
Admitted to stepdown on scheduled bronchodilators, azithromycin, and IV steroid: methylprednisolone 40 mg IV every 8 hours; glucose rose to 342 requiring insulin sliding scale.
Hyperglycemia managed with sliding scale plus short course of basal insulin; resolved as steroids tapered.
Volume status: History of heart failure with ejection fraction 30%; bilateral leg edema and 3 kg weight increase this week. Diuresed with IV furosemide, net -3.9 L, weight down 3.1 kg by HD5.
Oxygen weaned to room air during the day by HD5. Ambulated 150 feet on HD6 with SpO2 90% on room air.
CXR showed hyperinflation and mild congestion, no consolidation. Troponin flat, ECG without ischemic change.
PT evaluated and cleared for home with rollator.
DISCHARGE EXAM: T 36.8, HR 78, BP 126/72, RR 18, SpO2 92% on room air. Lungs with rare faint wheeze, trace ankle edema.
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
Prednisone 40 mg PO daily x 3 more days then stop
Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily; budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 two puffs BID
Albuterol MDI 2 puffs q4h PRN with spacer
Furosemide 40 mg PO daily
Carvedilol 6.25 mg PO BID, lisinopril 10 mg PO daily
Metformin 500 mg PO BID resumed
Home O2 2L NC nocturnal as before
INSTRUCTIONS:
Daily weights, call for gain of 2 kg in 2 days or worsening leg swelling.
Check blood sugars twice daily while on prednisone; call if above 300.
Return for increased work of breathing, confusion, or fever.
FOLLOW-UP:
Pulmonary clinic in 2 weeks, primary care in 5 days, cardiology in 4 weeks.
Discharge instructions reviewed with pt, wife, and daughter at bedside; teach-back on inhaler use completed with RT.
